paper.title: Sharper Regret Bounds for Time-Varying Gaussian Process Bandits with Constant Exploration

settings.name_in_paper: Time-varying Gaussian process (TV-GP) bandit with drift parameter epsilon
unmapped: Reward functions evolve by the Markov GP recursion f_{t+1} = sqrt(1-eps) f_t + sqrt(eps) g_{t+1}, with g_t i.i.d. GP(0,k_S); drift rate eps in (0,1] (not a variation budget V_T)
The learner knows the drift parameter eps (it is used in the posterior)
Regret is measured against the per-round maximiser x_t^* of f_t (dynamic regret)
settings.definition_quote: f_1(x)=g_1(x),\qquad f_{t+1}(x)=\sqrt{1-\epsilon}\,f_t(x)+\sqrt{\epsilon}\,g_{t+1}(x), ... y_t = f_t(x_t) + z_t, z_t \sim \mathcal{N}(0,\sigma^2) i.i.d. ... r_t := f_t(x_t^\star)-f_t(x_t)

symbols.gamma_tilde_T: time-varying maximum information gain under the time-decayed kernel
symbols.a: constant in the derivative tail bound
symbols.b: constant in the derivative tail bound
symbols.mu_w: expected spatial span E[sup f_t - inf f_t]
symbols.sigma_w: sub-Gaussian variance proxy of the span W_t

conditions: S subset of [0,r]^d compact and convex
derivative tail bound (Assumption 1) with constants a >= 1, b > 0
tuning: delta in (0,1), tau in N+ are analysis parameters

source.label: thrm:improved_regret
source.quote: If the evaluation points $\{x_t\}_{t=1}^T$ are selected according to Algorithm~\ref{alg:TV} with any constant exploration parameter satisfying \beta \ge 2(\log(6/\delta)+ d\log(\tau)). then the expected cumulative regret satisfies \mathbb{E}[R_T] \le \sqrt{C_1 T \beta\,\tilde{\gamma}_T}+ T C_2 + T\delta C_3

results.notes: The expectation is over the GP prior, the noise and the algorithm, and regret is against the per-round maximiser, so it is recorded as Bayesian dynamic regret. The bound is linear in T. The algorithm does not use T, so the result is recorded as anytime.

symbols.omega: failure probability of the reported bound

source.label: prop:realized_regret
source.quote: Assume the setting and parameter choices of Theorem~\ref{thrm:improved_regret}. For any target failure probability $\omega \in (0,1)$, the realized cumulative regret $R_T$ satisfies the following bound with probability at least $1-\omega$: R_T \le U_T + \frac{T \delta C_3}{\omega}.

results.notes: U_T = sqrt(C_1 T beta gamma_tilde_T) + T C_2. The probability is over the prior and the noise.

symbols.eps_drift: drift parameter epsilon of the TV-GP model

conditions: gamma_tilde_T / T = O_tilde(eps^alpha) with alpha > 0 in the regime considered

source.label: cor:prescribed_confidence
source.quote: Then, with probability at least $1-\omega$, \frac{R_T}{T} = \widetilde{\mathcal O}\left(\epsilon^{\alpha/2}\sqrt{1+\log(1/\omega)+\log(1/\epsilon)}\right). In particular, $\beta$ remains independent of $t$ and $T$.

results.notes: The paper bounds the average regret R_T/T; the expression is multiplied by T so that it bounds total regret. The algorithm uses omega and epsilon to set beta.

symbols.q: exponent of the static maximum information gain, gamma_N = O_tilde(N^q), q in [0,1)

conditions: static maximum information gain gamma_N = O_tilde(N^q) with q in [0,1)
tuning: delta = eps^(alpha/2), tau = ceil(eps^(-alpha/2)) with alpha = 2(1-q)/(4-q)

source.label: eq:regret_main_rate
source.quote: Balancing the remaining terms in Theorem~\ref{thrm:improved_regret} as in Section~\ref{subsec:Opt_beta_eps} then yields \frac{\mathbb E[R_T]}{T} = \widetilde{\mathcal O}\left(\epsilon^{\frac{1-q}{4-q}}\right).

results.notes: Derived in the main text by combining Theorem 1 with Corollary 7; it is not a formal theorem. The average-regret rate is multiplied by T. Special cases: for the squared exponential kernel (q=0) the average regret is O_tilde(eps^(1/4)); for the Matern kernel with nu > 2 it is O_tilde(eps^(2nu/(8nu+3d))).
